audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagreed with the 4310-game packet in four rows and with the mirror: level 1 and levels 4-5 were 'Skill' when Renekton wins them, level 6 was 'Skill' when Depth Charge decides it, and both item rows were Renekton when Iceborn Gauntlet flips the 1v1.
audit.why: The page's own whys already say it: whys[4] tells you not to start a 6 all-in into his R, whys[5] says take short trades because his item spike lands with yours, whys[6] says stop trying to 1v1 him. Meanwhile the mirror on the Nautilus side already set rows 0 and 3 to Renekton, 4 to Nautilus, 5 to Skill, 6 to Nautilus in both layers.
audit.corrected: Chart becomes Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Nautilus, Skill, Nautilus in both layers as one atomic group, with ratings moved to match.

audit.why: Spikes already read levels 2-3, 4-5, Depth Charge at 6, and Iceborn Gauntlet at 2+ items, which is the real shape of the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: The interaction that decides every all-in was never stated: empowered Ruthless Predator at 50+ Fury DESTROYS damage shields on the target, so Titan's Wrath does not absorb your burst — it is deleted. The page only ever mentioned the stun going from 0.75s to 1.5s.
audit.why: Riot's Renekton W text: 'destroying damage shields on the target, dealing high physical damage, and stunning them for 1.5 seconds'. Nautilus W: 'Nautilus gains a temporary Shield', flat 12s cooldown. The missingInteractions file flags shield-absorbs-burst here, and the mirror's point-4 finding is the same interaction from his side.
audit.corrected: Say it in the do's, in Key Ability Interactions, and in what he wants: he must cash Titan's Wrath before your empowered W lands, because at 50+ Fury the shield is removed outright. Dredge Line's 14s rank-1 cooldown is now a number on the page.
sources: kit: Nautilus W text and cd 12

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 advice told you flatly not to step into auto range, which does not square with giving Renekton the level-1 row.
audit.why: Staggering Blow roots only on his first attack against a given target, so the counterplay is short bursts and stepping out, not refusing to trade at all. Renekton's Fury autos are the stronger level-1 tool.
audit.corrected: whys[0] now names Staggering Blow and prescribes short bursts with a step-out before it can re-apply.

edits.before: Nautilus's passive roots you on the first auto — do not step into auto range at level 1, farm at Q tip and build Fury safely before committing anything.
edits.after: Your Fury autos out-trade him, but Staggering Blow roots on his first hit against you — trade in short bursts and step out before he can re-apply it.

edits.before: Nautilus wastes Dredge Line (Hook) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: At 50+ Fury your W destroys Titan's Wrath outright and stuns 1.5s — commit then.

edits.before: Absorb your early all-ins on his tank base stats and survive until Iceborn Gauntlet turns extended fights into slows and roots
edits.after: Pop Titan's Wrath (12s flat) before your W lands — an empowered W at 50+ Fury deletes the shield outright and stuns 1.5s

edits.before: Track Nautilus's Dredge Line (Hook): His only engage. Dodge it. When it is down — W-stun + Q him.
edits.after: Dodge Dredge Line (14s at rank 1); at 50+ Fury your W deletes Titan's Wrath and stuns 1.5s.

notes: All five chart rows are proposed as matched full/content pairs in one group, matching both the packet and the already-audited Nautilus side. Not asserted: whether Dredge Line can yank Renekton mid-dash or whether the empowered W stun is shortened by tenacity from his items — neither is answerable from Riot's text. The existing claim in 'late' that Iceborn Gauntlet slows you 'out of your E dash' is a slow, not a dash cancel, and reads as stronger than it is; I left the wording alone rather than rewrite on an unverified mechanic.
